correctness.rationale: The Laurent substitution X=z+a/z is injective on polynomials and gives Frobenius reduction. Differentiating the Laurent identity and squaring yields the normalized derivative identity; cancellation and monicity give D_p'/p congruent to (X^2-4a)^((p-1)/2). On ordinary discs the higher Taylor terms vanish after normalization and reduction modulo p, so uniquely lifting the unit linear map gives all outputs in the depth-two ball and the asserted fibers. For a square unit a=b^2, homogeneity reduces to parameter 1. With m=(p-1)/2, the geometric sum z^(-m)(z^p-1)/(z-1) proves the square factorization of D_p(Y,1)-2; that factor is p at Y=2 and has derivative divisible by p there since m>=2. Thus the normalized exceptional map is the identity modulo p as a polynomial, giving depth-three balls at the stated centers and p^2 fibers for k>=3. Reduction modulo p keeps branches disjoint, including the boundary precisions k=1 and k=2. For p=3 and a=1 the exceptional normalized map at +2 is u(1+u)^2, with two values modulo 3; the negative branch contributes two and the ordinary branch nine modulo 81, confirming the stated exclusion.
